newsitem.title: USA: Carolina First, First Southeast to merge.
newsitem.headline: Carolina First, First Southeast to merge.

text.p: Carolina First Corp and First Southeast Financial Corp said Tuesday they had signed a definitive agreement to merge in a stock swap worth $65 million.
They said holding company First Southeast will merge its First Federal Savings and Loan Association of Anderson, S.C., into Carolina First's Carolina First Bank.
First Southeast shareholders will receive one share of Carolina First common for each share of First Southeast, they said.
Carolina First will issue 4.4 million shares as part the deal, which is valued at $14.75 per First Southeast share, or about $65 million in total, the companies said.
Carolina First and First Southeast said the merger will bring Carolina First's assets to more than $2.0 billion. Market capitalization will total about $250 million, they said.
On March 31 First Southeast had about $335 million in assets, $261 million in loans, and $283 million in deposits, they said.
Carolina First is a bank holding company based in Greenville, S.C.
